name: Early retiree 35-yr
description: Age-50 client walks in with $1.5M and wants to retire today, spending $5,500/month in today's dollars for 35 years (a 4.4% initial withdrawal rate — just above the classic 4% rule). Runs on the 1926–2026 block bootstrap, so the plan is stress-tested against the Depression, 1970s stagflation, and 2008. The live success rate answers the only question that matters: 'Do I make it to 85?'

name: Pre-retiree 10-yr glidepath
description: Age-55 client, $650k saved, contributing $2,500/month, plans to retire at 65 and draw $4,500/month. Equity allocation glides from 90% down to 60% over the 10 working years — the classic 'de-risk into retirement' conversation. The de-risked sleeve is real: each simulated month blends that month's historical equity return with the SAME month's 10-year Treasury return (month-aligned Shiller blocks), and holds 60/40 through retirement — so the success-rate lift you see is actual bond diversification, not a cash-floor fudge. Toggle the glidepath off to see what staying 100% equity costs in sequence-of-returns risk.

name: Fat-tail stress
description: For the client who says 'markets always come back.' Same prudent plan — $1.25M, $4,200/month (a textbook 4.0% initial rate), 30 years — but the return engine swaps Gaussian noise for Student-t (ν=5) innovations, matching the fat tails actually observed in a century of monthly data. Honest expectation-setting: over 360 monthly steps the central limit theorem washes most of that out — the measured terminal success gap vs GBM is ≈0.03pp (estimator noise), NOT a big drop. What fat tails actually change is the SHAPE of the journey: deeper, sharper crashes inside the paths (watch the worst-decile drawdown and the cone's left tail), which is exactly the experience that makes clients abandon a plan at the bottom.

name: High-withdrawal cautionary
description: The cautionary tale every advisor needs: client with $1.2M insists on $8,000/month — an 8% initial withdrawal rate, double the 4% rule. Watch the cone: the failure flag lights up across a wide swath of histories, and the median failure year tells the client roughly when the money runs out. Perfect segue to the safe-withdrawal-rate stat, which computes the withdrawal that history would have supported 90% of the time.

name: Accumulation only
description: The 30-year-old just starting out: $25k saved, $1,500/month going in, no withdrawals for 30 years. No retirement-phase failure risk — this view is about the distribution of outcomes. Drag the contribution slider and watch the whole cone lift; the p5/p95 spread makes the case that time in the market, not timing, dominates the outcome.
